notes:
Summary: enterprise insurance account evaluating Redwood Dedicated for claims automation (chat + reranking + embeddings). Primary ask: validated reserved capacity sizing and transparent unit economics by commit level. Heavy security/compliance constraints — must support VPC + customer KMS, SOC2/ISO reports required.

Key requirements (from RFP/meetings):
- Workloads: claims-assistant chat (context windows ~512 tokens), document embeddings for policy search, reranking for fraud detection.
- Latency targets: chat p95 <= 150ms (512 tokens), tail behavior important; embedding latency p95 <= 120ms for single-vector queries.
- Throughput targets: chat steady-state 150 reqs/sec (peak 350 RPS burst), embeddings 400-600 QPS during business hours.
- Availability: 99.9% SLA target for Dedicated region; legal wants credit structure for missed SLOs.
- Data: PHI-adjacent (claims info) — data residency and audit logs mandatory.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit economics beat cloud passthrough + overhead by >=20%.

Cost modeling results (workshop 2026-03-07) — illustrative, for negotiation and internal procurement pack: 
- Assumptions used across scenarios: average request = 800 tokens (chat roundtrip + context), embeddings request = 256 tokens; working month = 30 days. Utilization = effective GPU compute utilization after batching/caching.

Scenario A (Conservative commit)
- Commit: 2 x 80GB GPUs (equiv. reserve for critical region)
- Estimated monthly platform cost (list): $35,000
- Expected sustained throughput: ~80 RPS chat + 200 QPS embeddings during business hours
- Utilization assumption: 40%
- Estimated tokens/month supported @40% util: 400M tokens
- Unit economics: $35,000 / 400M = $0.0000875 per token -> $0.0875 per 1k tokens
- Comments: lowest entry, good for proof-of-value but unit cost above target; fine for narrow pilot.

Scenario B (Mid-commit, recommended for production)
- Commit: 4 x 80GB GPUs
- Estimated monthly platform cost (negotiated list): $60,000 (open to discussion on multi-year pricing)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~200 RPS chat + 450 QPS embeddings peak capacity with autoscale/burst policy to spare
- Utilization assumption: 60% (aggressive batching, prefix caching for frequently hit policies)
- Estimated tokens/month supported @60% util: 1.5B tokens
- Unit economics: $60,000 / 1.5B = $0.00004 per token -> $0.04 per 1k tokens
- Comments: hits procurement's target of ~20–30% savings vs cloud-hosted per-token pricing benchmarks; best tradeoff for steady production.

Scenario C (Aggressive commit for scale & discounts)
- Commit: 8 x 80GB GPUs
- Estimated monthly platform cost (discounted commit): $110,000
- Expected utilization: 70% (more caching + request consolidation)
- Estimated tokens/month supported @70% util: 3.0B tokens
- Unit economics: $110,000 / 3.0B = $0.0000367 per token -> $0.0367 per 1k tokens
- Comments: lowest marginal token cost, requires strong commit and sustained volume; procurement wants demand forecast proof (12-mo true-up) before approving.

Negotiation / SLA asks from Pallisade: 
- Need explicit throughput guarantees at 95th and 99th percentiles (requests/sec sustained for N minutes) with automatic fallback model variants if capacity constrained.
- Latency SLO tied to per-route model (chat vs embeddings), credits if p95 exceeds threshold 3x in month.
- Autoscaling burst allowance (x2 for 15-minute windows) included in contract or pre-authorized on-call escalation flow.
- Annual usage true-up and option to convert unused commit to credits for other regions.

Open technical questions (blocking procurement):
- Exact pricing sheet tied to GPU type (A100 vs equivalent), and whether quantized model variants (8-bit) are supported for production inference with Redwood optimize profiles.
- Details on network egress cost assumptions for VPC/private deployments.
- What telemetry/data returns to Redwood default control plane in Private mode; need on-prem telemetry redaction options.

Action items / next steps (short):
- Provide formal 2-week Dedicated POC quote and schedule (SE/Priya to propose windows) — POC must include: representative claims corpus (anonymized), end-to-end latency measurements, prewarming / KV cache tests.
- Legal to draft SLA appendix with throughput/latency SLOs & credit formula (Jordan + Redwood legal).
- Security to validate KMS/HSM integration flow and sign off on audit log retention policy.
- Procurement to confirm budget band and preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly).

Representative quotes from Pallisade stakeholders: 
- "We need predictable unit economics—if we commit, it must materially reduce our per-token cost vs cloud bursts." — Director, ML Platforms
- "Tail latency kills our adjuster UX; p95 matters more than average." — Head of Claims Automation
